description:
FOUND s509 (Fable, 2026-10-06), the speed review.  docs/speed-review-s509.md; measurements and profiles in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/speed/ (prof.pl ROW... -> ROW.pl, ROW.lisp, ROW.prof; main b43188b5, gen v2-4280, load 5-6, best of 3-5)

MEASURED (2 M calls each, programs pr-*.pl in that directory, perl -> main):
     print {$fh} "x\n"      0.089 -> 0.292   3.3x          print $fh "x", "\n"     0.129 -> 0.364   2.8x
     print $fh "x\n"        0.092 -> 0.291   3.2x          print "x\n" (STDOUT)    0.074 -> 0.233   3.2x
     print $fh $x           0.093 -> 0.288   3.1x          print $fh "v=$i\n"      0.149 -> 0.578   3.9x
PROFILE (fhprint.prof): `%p-write-list` 47 % total; `p-flatten-args` 13 %, `%make-p-box` 8 %, `vector-to-list` 3 %,
`%p-resolve-fh` 14 %, `length` 6 %, the byte output itself 9 %.  The emission is `(p-print :fh $fh (p-esc "x\n"))` -- the
general &rest form for every spelling.

DIRECTION (needs a SHORT DESIGN NOTE before code): when every argument FORM is a scalar at compile time (a literal, an
interpolated string / p-string-concat, a scalar variable, a scalar-valued builtin) the expansion can call an N-scalar entry
(1, 2, 3 arguments, else the general one): no rest list, no flatten, no box.  It must keep ONE path for the semantics --
`$,` and `$\` (read once per call), a tied handle, an in-memory handle, the SELECTED handle for the no-handle form, the
`:utf8` / encoding layers, `print`'s return value, the closed-handle case.  A Kind-A gate in Pl/Passes.pm (named, switchable
by PCL_OPT) if the decision is made in the compiler; a compiler macro if it can be made from the forms alone.

EXPECTED: -40 to -50 % on fhprint and on any output-heavy loop (the flatten + box + list + lookup share of the profile).
NOT cheap in the sense of #2770: medium.  The bar includes the everyday corpus byte-identical and io/print.t, io/say.t.
subject: PERF, MEASURED s509 (lever B): EVERY `print` is 3.1-3.9x perl (145 ns vs 45 ns per call) -- one string argument is flattened into a vector, boxed, turned into a list and the handle resolved, before 2 bytes are written; a compile-time arm for all-scalar arguments
